experiment.title: 07 - Evidence hidden across multiple sources
experiment.question: What is the final approved budget for Project Orion, and when was it approved?

documents.title: Project Orion - Project Charter
documents.content:
Project Orion - Project Charter
Date: 2026-03-04
Owner: Transformation Office

Objective: Consolidate customer onboarding workflows across three operating regions.
Scope: Identity verification, case routing, exception handling, and reporting.
Target deployment: Q2 2027. Sponsor: Chief Operations Officer.
The charter describes the project's intended outcomes but does not authorize expenditure.
A detailed cost baseline will be maintained separately by Finance.

Milestones:
- April: initial requirements
- June: solution selection
- August: revised delivery plan
- October: integration readiness

The sponsor requested that all funding decisions be documented in the steering committee decision log. Project status reports are informational and must not be used as evidence of approval.

documents.title: Project Orion - Initial Budget Proposal
documents.content:
Project Orion - Initial Budget Proposal
Date: 2026-04-12
Status: Draft for discussion

Estimated implementation cost: EUR 2.6 million.
The estimate includes EUR 1.1 million for engineering, EUR 0.7 million for integration, EUR 0.5 million for external services, and EUR 0.3 million for contingency.
This is a planning estimate, not an approved funding baseline.

Assumptions:
- Existing data contracts remain unchanged.
- No additional regulatory certification is required.
- Vendor onboarding can begin in June.

Finance noted that the contingency may need revision following the supplier review. The proposed figure is retained here for historical comparison only.

documents.title: Project Orion - Steering Committee Minutes
documents.content:
Project Orion - Steering Committee Minutes
Meeting date: 2026-09-18
Location: Conference Room C / video call
Chair: Programme Sponsor
Attendees: Finance Director, Delivery Lead, Procurement Lead, Risk Officer

Agenda item 1: Delivery readiness. The team reported that interface specifications were signed off, with two integration risks remaining open.
Agenda item 2: Procurement. The preferred vendor was asked to provide an updated implementation schedule. Contract award remains subject to procurement controls.
Agenda item 3: Funding baseline. The committee reviewed the revised financial baseline circulated by Finance under revision BR-07. Members confirmed that the superseded April estimate must no longer be used for reporting.

Decision SC-2026-0918-04: The steering committee approved the Project Orion funding baseline identified as BR-07 on 18 September 2026.

Action: Finance to publish the approved baseline in the project reporting pack. The minutes record the decision and baseline identifier; the detailed monetary amount is maintained in the Finance revision register.
Agenda item 4: Resourcing. Recruitment of two integration specialists may proceed within the approved staffing envelope.
Next meeting: 2026-10-16.

documents.title: Project Orion - Risk Register
documents.content:
Project Orion - Risk Register
Updated: 2026-09-22

R-014: Supplier transition could delay delivery by six weeks. Likelihood medium, impact high. Mitigation: dual-track onboarding.
R-021: Data migration test coverage below target. Likelihood medium, impact medium. Mitigation: add reconciliation checks.
R-028: A potential EUR 400,000 schedule exposure is tracked as a risk estimate; this is not a project budget or funding decision.
R-033: Additional accessibility testing may be needed for the reporting dashboard.

Risk exposure figures represent potential future costs, not authorized funding. The register is not the source of record for budget approvals.

documents.title: Project Orion - Procurement Overview
documents.content:
Project Orion - Procurement Overview
Updated: 2026-09-15

Supplier A: Indicative services quote EUR 980,000, subject to commercial negotiation.
Supplier B: Indicative platform quote EUR 620,000, excluding taxes and implementation support.
Supplier C: Optional migration tooling EUR 190,000.

The procurement plan lists commercial quotations and contract status. None of these quotes constitutes a complete project budget or an approval of project funding.

Procurement checkpoints: due diligence, data-processing review, contract redlines, purchase order release. The team will not issue purchase orders until the funding baseline has been approved.

documents.title: Project Orion - Finance Budget Revision Register
documents.content:
Project Orion - Finance Budget Revision Register
Maintained by: Corporate Finance
Last updated: 2026-09-19

Revision history:
BR-03 | 2026-04-12 | Initial planning estimate | EUR 2.60 million | Draft
BR-05 | 2026-07-28 | Supplier and integration adjustment | EUR 2.74 million | Under review
BR-06 | 2026-08-30 | Contingency scenario | EUR 3.10 million | Scenario only

Reconciliation note: BR-05 included an integration allowance that was revised after technical due diligence. BR-06 was prepared for stress testing and was not submitted as the funding baseline.

BR-07 | 2026-09-16 | Revised funding baseline | EUR 2.85 million | Submitted for steering committee decision

BR-07 breakdown: delivery engineering EUR 1.20 million; integration EUR 0.80 million; external services EUR 0.55 million; contingency EUR 0.30 million. Total EUR 2.85 million.

This register records the value and identity of each revision. Formal approval decisions are documented in steering committee minutes rather than inferred from a revision's presence in this register.

documents.title: Project Orion - Team Capacity Plan
documents.content:
Project Orion - Team Capacity Plan
Updated: 2026-09-10

Delivery squad: 8 engineers, 2 QA specialists, 1 delivery manager.
Expected external specialist allocation: 110 person-days in Q4.
A separate resource scenario assumes EUR 420,000 in staff-related costs, which is not the total project budget.

Dependencies: security review in October, integration testing in November, operations handover in December. Capacity assumptions are provisional and do not establish funding approval.

documents.title: Project Orion - Monthly Status Report
documents.content:
Project Orion - Monthly Status Report
Reporting period: August 2026
Overall status: Amber

Delivery: 72% of planned design milestones complete.
Costs: Working forecast EUR 2.74 million based on BR-05; Finance is preparing an updated baseline.

Next steps: finalize vendor estimates, close integration assumptions, and present revised baseline to the September committee.

documents.title: Project Orion - Internal Email Thread
documents.content:
Project Orion - Internal Email Thread
Subject: Orion figures for board pack

2026-08-26, Delivery Lead to Finance:
Can we still use EUR 2.6m in the September slides? It is the number most stakeholders remember.

2026-08-27, Finance Analyst:
Please do not label EUR 2.6m as approved. It was the original draft. BR-05 currently reflects EUR 2.74m, and another revision is being prepared.

2026-09-12, Programme Office:
For the next board pack, please use a placeholder until the steering committee records a formal funding decision. The email chain is not the approval record.

2026-09-14, Delivery Lead:
Understood. We will keep the old number only in the historical comparison appendix.

documents.title: Project Orion - Funding Governance Policy
documents.content:
Project Orion - Funding Governance Policy
Effective: 2026-01-01

Section 2. Authority: Project budgets above EUR 1 million require a recorded steering committee decision.
Section 3. Evidence: A valid funding claim must identify the committee decision and the associated Finance baseline revision. Neither a budget proposal nor a Finance revision entry alone proves approval.
Section 4. Reporting: Where multiple revisions exist, reports must use the revision explicitly authorized by the committee.
Section 5. Audit trail: Retain meeting minutes, revision register, and supporting quotations as separate records.

Example (unrelated to Orion): Project Vega had a EUR 3.4 million scenario but a EUR 3.0 million approved baseline. Figures from different projects must never be combined.

semantic_reference.answer: The final approved budget for Project Orion is EUR 2.85 million, approved by the steering committee on 18 September 2026. Approval applies to baseline BR-07, whose value is recorded in the Finance revision register. Accept equivalent wording, but require both the amount and approval date, with evidence connecting the approval decision to BR-07 and BR-07 to EUR 2.85 million. Do not confuse older proposals, forecasts, scenarios, supplier quotes, or risk estimates with the approved baseline.
